text.p: Portuguese bonds firmed but dealers said that trading was muted ahead of U.S. February CPI and that market sentiment remained basically bearish.
"Futures are seeing a slight upward correction, helped by gains in Italy, but cash bonds are treading very cautiously," said one trader.

"Nothing's changed. We don't know if the single currency will be delayed and we're still worried about a possible hike in U.S. rates. The escudo is steady but there is no sign of a strong recovery," said another dealer.
Dealers said that 10-year bond yields would probably remain at just below seven percent.

"The June 97 futures contract is meeting resistence at 105.50 and has support at 105. It may go a little higher today but any strong rise would simply encourage people to sell again. The negative trend remains," said one analyst.
At 1300 GMT the escudo was quoted at 100.64/66 per mark, little changed from the opening.
Tomorrow/next rates were steady at 6.20/6.22 percent.
